title: Oncall abuse triage and quota adjustments - notes Q1 2026
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working on-call note + draft runbook fragment capturing a couple of recent small-to-medium abuse/quota incidents we saw in Nov 2025–Jan 2026. The goal is to: 1) capture what we observed, 2) document immediate tactical mitigations that helped, 3) propose adjustments to quota/rate-limit rules and WAF heuristics, and 4) list follow-ups (owners + rough ETA). Treat as operational notes (not a full postmortem).

Summary of incidents observed (high-level):
- Incident A (2025-11-28): Suspected API key leakage causing systematic high-volume generation requests against embeddings endpoint from a narrow set of client keys. Average RPS for those keys spiked from 0.2 -> 120 RPS per key over a 10-minute window. Generated a broad capacity pressure on the embedding pool and raised tail latencies.
- Incident B (2026-01-09): Traffic flood from a small botnet pattern originating across 14 /24 blocks. Requests were low token-length but extreme QPS for chat completion route; WAF blocked ~45% after rule tuning.
- Related observation (ongoing): Several customers hit unexpected quota errors when we applied emergency soft-limits; need smoother customer communication and smarter exceptions.

Detection signals that mattered:
- Alert: high-err-rate-on-embedding-backend (fired at 11:06 UTC) — correlated with sudden KV cache churn and GPU mempressure.
- Dashboard: per-key RPS heatmap (top keys by 1m RPS) — critical to pinpoint leaked key(s).
- WAF/Firewall telemetry: repeated identical User-Agent + header fingerprint from many IPs (botnet pattern).
- Billing/usage: abrupt token-counts on keys that were previously dormant.

Key metrics observed (approx):
- Peak RPS (per offending key): 100–140 RPS
- Aggregate embedding token rate: ~3.2M tokens/min at peak
- 95p latency (embedding): increased from 48ms -> 420ms during incident A
- Error rate (5xx) on routing service: jumped from 0.3% -> 6.8%

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 11:10 UTC: Identified suspect keys via per-key heatmap and `kadm list-keys --top-rps`.
- 11:12 UTC: Applied per-key hard throttle via api-gateway rule: set max-requests-per-minute=300 for offending keys (soft cut).
- 11:20 UTC: Escalated to emergency global embedding-burst-throttle (global soft cap at 12k RPS) to protect tail latency.
- 11:25 UTC: For some keys with clear leaked behavior we rotated API keys (issued new keys + disabled old) and triggered customer-notify email template (draft in Confluence).
- For Incident B we iterated WAF rule: added heuristic to block requests with UA regex + high QPS and implemented bot-challenge (captcha redirect for suspicious flows).

What worked and what didn't:
- Worked: Per-key RPS heatmap + ability to apply per-key throttles from the gateway were lifesavers. Rolling global soft cap prevented more severe latency degradation.
- Partially worked: WAF tuning reduced malicious traffic but initially had high false positives (blocked a few legitimate scrapers we rely on for research). We adjusted criteria after CS flagged 3 customers.
- Didn't work: No automated 'suspend-and-ask' workflow for keys that hit anomalous token growth. We had to manually rotate keys and send notices. Also, our customer-facing quota-error messages were opaque, leading to support volume.

Proposed runbook additions (draft steps, to be refined):
1) Initial Triage (first 10 minutes):
   - Verify alert -> open incident channel (sre-abuse)
   - Pull per-key 1m RPS and top-50 IPs; snapshot top headers (UA, Referer, X-Forwarded-For)
   - Check recent key creation/rotation events (kadm logs) to spot accidental leak in commit history / chat logs
2) Immediate Containment (10–30 minutes):
   - If per-key RPS > 50x baseline for > 5m: apply temporary per-key throttle of max-requests-per-minute = max(300, baseline*10)
content_continued:
- Apply global soft cap on the affected model pool if aggregate CPU/GPU mempressure > 70%
   - If IP clusters emerge (>10 unique requests from /24 in 5m), push WAF rule to challenge/count/block as appropriate
3) Key-rotation & Customer comms (15–60 minutes):
   - For confirmed leaked keys: rotate, disable old, create customer-notify draft (ops-cs template)
   - Provide CS with mitigation summary and ETA for longer-term quota relaxation if needed
4) Recovery & De-escalation (30–180 minutes):
   - Gradually relax global soft cap when 95p latency returns to normal for 10 consecutive minutes
   - Re-enable legitimate scrapers if flagged and add allowlist entries with expiration
5) Post-incident follow-ups (owner + ETA):
   - Create ticket to implement automated suspend-and-ask workflow (owner: Liam O'Connor, ETA: 3 weeks)
   - Improve customer-facing quota messages with actionable steps (owner: Mae Chen, ETA: 2 weeks)

Sample commands / snippets we used (operational):
- List keys by RPS: `kadm stats --window=1m --sort=rps | head -n 20`
- Apply gateway throttle (temporary): `gwctl throttle set --key=KEY_ID --rpm=300 --expires=60m --reason=\"suspected-leak\"`
- Rotate key (devops shim): `kadm rotate --key=KEY_ID --notify-cs=true`
- Add WAF rule (edge): `wafctl add-rule --name=\"bot-high-qps-ua-v1\" --match=\"ua_regex:BotScraper.* AND qps>50\" --action=challenge`

Heuristics for future automated detection (candidate rules):
- Per-key token growth > 10x baseline in 5m AND top-5 request bodies are identical -> mark as probable-key-leak
- Identical prompt + identical prompt-length across > 50 requests from > 10 IPs within 2m -> flag as mass-scrape attempt
- New key created within 24h + > 1k requests in first hour -> require manual verification (suspicious onboarding spike)

WAF rule tuning notes (lessons learned):
- Initial regex-based blocking led to >5% false positives; prefer multi-signal rules (UA + IP entropy + qps + token-count)
- Maintain allowlist of verified scrapers with TTLs; require owners to re-verify every 90 days
- Capture and store blocked request samples in a short-term buffer for CS review (48h retention)

Open questions / risks:
- Rate-limit granularity: should we add per-route token-based throttles (tokens/min) vs request-count-based? Token-based would better protect cost but is slightly more complex to enforce at the edge.
- Customer experience: how to automatically surface 'we throttled you' messages in-app so legitimate customers aren't surprised by opaque 429s.
- Abuse attribution: how often do leaked keys map to internal secrets mismanagement vs user sharing vs credential stuffing? We need better telemetry linking key issuance context.

Action items (concrete):
- [Liam] Implement suspend-and-ask prototype in gateway (auto-suspend when abnormal growth detected) — ETA 2026-03-10
- [Mae] Draft improved quota-error text + doc for CS (include steps to rotate keys) — ETA 2026-02-24
- [Diego] Add short-term blocked-request buffer in WAF for CS review (48h retention, sample=100/day) — ETA 2026-02-17
- [Priya] Run tabletop for on-call rotation with a simulated key-leak scenario (30m drill) — ETA 2026-03-01

Notes to future reader:
- This is intentionally fragmentary — keep iterative edits here. When we have enough signal, convert to a canonical playbook page in Confluence and link back.
- If you are oncall and see a spike, start with the per-key heatmap; it will often show the offender before IP-level analysis does.

Appendix: quick checklist (for copy/paste during incidents)
- Open channel: #sre-abuse
- Run: `kadm stats --window=1m --sort=rps`
- If top key > 50x baseline: `gwctl throttle set --key=KEY_ID --rpm=300 --expires=60m`
- If IP block cluster detected: `wafctl add-rule --name=temp-block-<ts> --match=ip_subnet:<block>/24 --action=block --expires=120m`
- Notify CS: paste incident ID + key id + mitigation steps

-- end of notes (draft) --
